newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden says to cease net forex borrowing in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sweden says to cease net forex borrowing in 1997.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Ministry on Thursday said the government had decided that foreign currency borrowing in 1997 would not exceed the amount of foreign currrency loans expiring during the year.
This means in effect that Sweden will cease net borrowing in foreign currrency next year.
"The National Debt Office will not borrow more in foreign currencies in calender 1997 than an amount corresponding to expiring foreign currency loans," the finance ministry said in a statement.
However, the National Debt Office could depart from this norm to some extent "depending on the situation on the international capital market", the ministry said.
It said the decision should be seen against the background of success in consolidating public finances, a process which had led to a substantial reduction in the state borrowing requirement.
The decision entails a further reduction in currency borrowing. State net borrowing in foreign currencies has fallen from 49 billion crowns in 1995 to an estimated 30 billion in 1996.
